The VAWT model had 3 blades with a NACA0021 airfoil profile.
The rotor diameter was 1.030 m and the span length was 1.456 m.
The solidity of the VAWT was 0.25.
The V-shaped blades were created by moving the blade middle cross-section along the tangential direction of the rotor.
The maximum enhancement in power coefficient occurred at ΔV = 0.6c, with a 24.1% increase compared to the baseline straight-bladed VAWT.
The influence of the V-shaped blades on the thrust coefficient was relatively small, with variations less than 4%.
The trailing-edge serrations generated less low-frequency noise compared to the straight-bladed VAWT.
A dumbbell-shaped noise directivity distribution was discovered for the first time in a VAWT.
The Reynolds number range for the simulations was 1.1 × 10^5 to 2.2 × 10^5.
The simulations for 8 revolutions took about 168 hours, and the acoustic calculations for another 2 revolutions took about 360 hours.
The power coefficient of the V-bladed wind turbine with trailing-edge serrations was about 28.3% higher than the original turbine.
The researchers investigated the use of trailing-edge serrations as a noise reduction technique for the VAWT.
The computational model was divided into a stationary domain and a rotational domain, using the sliding mesh technique.
The four regions defined in the model based on the azimuthal range of the blade were the upwind, leeward, downwind, and windward regions.
A total of 33 acoustic receivers were set up in the middle plane to cover the sound wave propagation.
